references.text: Pisga is also mentioned here as a vantage point overlooking the wilderness (Jeshimon), the same geographical area as Peor.
Balak also took Balaam to the top of Pisga earlier, another high point in the same mountain range as Peor.
Peor later became the place where Israel sinned by worshiping Baal-Peor, showing the significance of this location.
The incident at Peor is mentioned again as Balaam's counsel that led Israel into sin.
Beth-peor is mentioned as the place where Israel stayed in the valley, the same area as Peor.
Moses reminds the people of what the Lord did at Baal-Peor.
Moses was buried in the valley in the land of Moab, opposite Beth-peor.
The sin at Peor is mentioned as a warning to Israel.
The psalm refers to Israel binding themselves to Baal-Peor.
Hosea mentions Baal-Peor and Israel's shame there.
